title: Adding a Databricks resource type touches three registrations in mlflow/models/resources.py
answers: how do I add a new Databricks resource type for model serving
add a new resource dependency to logged model resources
new resource type not serialized to MLmodel resources YAML
declare a new Databricks dependency when logging a model
body:
Symptom: A newly declared Databricks dependency (e.g. a model-serving resource) is missing from the logged model's resources YAML or fails to round-trip when the model is loaded.
Root cause: Resource types are wired in three separate places in mlflow/models/resources.py: the ResourceType enum, a concrete class subclassing DatabricksResource with a `type` property, and the `resource_classes["databricks"]` map in _get_resource_class_by_type. Missing any one breaks serialization or deserialization.
Fix pattern: Add the enum member with its wire value, add a DatabricksX(DatabricksResource) class whose `type` returns that member and whose __init__ forwards to super(), and add `ResourceType.X.value: DatabricksX` to the map in _get_resource_class_by_type. Then extend tests/models/test_resources.py (a parametrized per-type test, plus the expected dicts in test_resources and test_resources_from_yaml).
Constraints: The existing resource types are untouched; add new types alongside them rather than renaming wire values. Do not change the serialized key of an existing type for backward compatibility.
applies: Applies to any new resource type under the 'databricks' target_uri in mlflow/models/resources.py; does not cover non-Databricks target URIs.
says: A declared cloud service dependency does not appear in the saved model resource configuration.
Serving resources attached to a logged model fail to reload when loading the model.
Allow logging models with a new type of backend serving dependency.
Cloud resource dependencies specified during model logging are dropped from the metadata package.
Saved model definitions do not retain newly configured cloud infrastructure requirements upon export.
search: Adding a new Databricks resource type under target_uri 'databricks' in mlflow/models/resources.py requires updating ResourceType, subclassing DatabricksResource with a type property, and registering in resource_classes['databricks'] in _get_resource_class_by_type. Missing any registration breaks serialization to MLmodel resources YAML or model reload round-tripping. Tests in tests/models/test_resources.py (per-type tests, test_resources, and test_resources_from_yaml) must be extended. Existing resource types and wire keys must not be changed, and non-Databricks target URIs are not covered.
